knowledgePoint.zh: AlphaGo如何将神经网络、强化学习与树搜索结合来征服围棋
knowledgePoint.en: How AlphaGo combined neural networks, RL, and tree search to master Go

recallIntro.zh: 你闭上眼，脑海中浮现出那天教室的场景。屏幕上是2016年3月的首尔四季酒店——李世石坐在棋盘一侧，另一侧是一个空空的座位和一只伸出来落子的机械手臂。西尔弗教授站在那幅画面前，眼神中闪动着一种你从未见过的光芒。
recallIntro.en: You close your eyes, and that day's classroom scene surfaces. The screen shows Seoul's Four Seasons Hotel in March 2016 — Lee Sedol sitting on one side of the board, an empty seat on the other side with a mechanical arm extending to place stones. Prof. Silver stands before that image, eyes shining with a light you've never seen before.

recallOutro.zh: 你回过神来。策略网络、价值网络、蒙特卡洛树搜索——三个组件像齿轮一样精密咬合。你想起西尔弗教授说的话：「AlphaGo不只是在下棋，它在用一种人类从未见过的方式思考。」那一刻的震撼至今没有消散。
recallOutro.en: You return to the present. Policy network, value network, Monte Carlo tree search — three components interlocking like precision gears. You recall Prof. Silver's words: 「AlphaGo wasn't just playing Go; it was thinking in a way humans had never seen before」. The awe of that moment hasn't faded.

text.zh: 今天的教室完全不同。大屏幕上循环播放着新闻报道的片段——「AI击败围棋世界冠军」「人类最后的堡垒被攻破」「这一天提前了十年到来」。评论席上的职业棋手们面露震惊。西尔弗教授走进教室时，脚步带着一种沉稳的骄傲。他没有立刻开口，而是站在屏幕前，安静地看了几秒钟那些新闻画面。
text.en: Today's classroom is completely different. The large screen loops news clips — 「AI defeats Go world champion」, 「Humanity's last bastion breached」, 「This day arrived ten years early」. Professional players in the commentary booth look stunned. Prof. Silver walks in with a stride of steady pride. He doesn't speak immediately, but stands before the screen, quietly watching the news footage for a few seconds.

text.zh: （转过身，面对大家）2016年3月9日到15日，首尔。我们的程序{AlphaGo}和世界冠军李世石进行了五局比赛。最终比分——4比1，AlphaGo胜。（停顿一下）在那之前，所有的专家预测都说，计算机在围棋上击败人类至少还需要十年。有些人说可能永远做不到。
text.en: (Turns to face everyone) March 9th to 15th, 2016, Seoul. Our program {AlphaGo} played five games against world champion Lee Sedol. Final score — 4 to 1, AlphaGo wins. (Pauses) Before that, every expert prediction said computers needed at least ten more years to beat humans at Go. Some said it might never happen.

text.zh: 为什么围棋被认为是AI最难攻克的棋类游戏？让我给你们一些数字。国际象棋的合法局面大约有10的47次方。围棋的合法局面大约有10的170次方。这个数字比整个可观测宇宙中的原子总数还要大——宇宙中的原子数大约是10的80次方。用传统的搜索算法逐一考察每种可能？数学上就已经排除了这种可能。
text.en: Why was Go considered the hardest board game for AI to crack? Let me give you some numbers. Chess has roughly 10 to the 47th power legal positions. Go has roughly 10 to the 170th power. That's more than the total number of atoms in the observable universe — which is about 10 to the 80th power. Using traditional search algorithms to examine every possibility? Mathematics alone rules that out.

text.zh: IBM的深蓝在1997年用搜索和评估函数击败了国际象棋世界冠军卡斯帕罗夫。但同样的方法在围棋上完全失败了。围棋的分支因子太大——每一步平均有250种合法落子，而国际象棋只有35种。用暴力搜索来下围棋，就像试图用一把尺子量出太平洋的宽度。
text.en: IBM's Deep Blue used search and evaluation functions to beat chess world champion Kasparov in 1997. But the same approach completely failed at Go. Go's branching factor is too large — each move averages 250 legal options, compared to 35 in chess. Using brute-force search to play Go is like trying to measure the Pacific Ocean's width with a ruler.

text.zh: 我们的方法完全不同。AlphaGo的核心包含三个组件，每一个都不可或缺。首先是{策略网络}：它看到一个棋盘局面，会输出每个位置的落子概率。本质上，它学会了「直觉」，能在几百个选项中快速缩小范围，找到最值得考虑的几步棋。
text.en: Our approach was completely different. AlphaGo's core contains three components, each indispensable. First: the {policy network} — it sees a board position and outputs the probability of playing at each position. In essence, it learned 「intuition」 — quickly narrowing down hundreds of options to find the few moves most worth considering.

text.zh: 第二个组件是{价值网络}。它看到一个局面，就会输出一个数字，代表黑方的胜率。如果输出0.7，就意味着在当前局面下，黑方有70%的概率获胜。这其实就是我们之前讲的价值函数在围棋中的具体应用，一个能「读懂」棋盘的神经网络。
text.en: The second component: the {value network} — it sees a position and outputs a single number: Black's probability of winning. If it outputs 0.7, that means in the current position, Black has a 70% chance of winning. This is the concrete application of the value function we discussed earlier to Go — a neural network that can 「read」 the board.

text.zh: 第三个组件：{蒙特卡洛树搜索}。它把策略网络和价值网络结合在一起。搜索的过程是这样的：从当前局面出发，策略网络告诉搜索算法「优先考虑哪些落子」；沿着选定的路径向前模拟几步，价值网络评估到达的局面有多好。反复这个过程成千上万次，最终选择在搜索中得到最高评价的那步棋。
text.en: The third component: {Monte Carlo tree search}. It brings the policy and value networks together. The search process works like this: starting from the current position, the policy network tells the search algorithm 「which moves to prioritize」; it simulates several steps forward along the chosen path, and the value network evaluates how good the resulting position is. Repeat this process thousands of times, and finally choose the move that received the highest evaluation across all searches.

text.zh: 你们知道这像什么吗？这就像人类棋手思考的过程。你看到一个局面，直觉告诉你「这几步值得考虑」（策略网络）。然后你在脑子里往前推演几步，评估可能的结果（搜索）。对于每个可能的结果，你的经验告诉你「这个局面对我有利还是不利」（价值网络）。AlphaGo做的事情和人类棋手本质上是一样的——只是它的计算速度快得多。
text.en: Do you know what this resembles? It's like how a human player thinks. You see a position, and intuition says 「these few moves are worth considering」 (policy network). Then you simulate ahead in your mind, evaluating possible outcomes (search). For each possible outcome, your experience tells you 「is this position favorable or unfavorable」 (value network). What AlphaGo does is essentially the same as a human player — it just calculates much faster.

text.zh: AlphaGo的三个组件包括策略网络、价值网络和蒙特卡洛树搜索。你觉得哪个是最关键的？
text.en: Of AlphaGo's three components — policy network, value network, Monte Carlo tree search — which do you think is the most critical?

text.zh: 策略网络——没有好的直觉来缩小搜索范围，搜索根本无法展开
text.en: The policy network — without good intuition to narrow the search, the search can't even begin

text.zh: 策略网络确实是搜索的起点。没有它，蒙特卡洛树搜索就必须在250个选项中盲目探索，效率极低。我们的策略网络经过训练，它推荐的前五步棋中，包含人类专业棋手实际落子的概率超过85%。这意味着搜索可以集中火力在最有希望的路径上。但单独的策略网络，如果不做搜索，棋力大约只有业余五段水平。搜索仍然是必要的。
text.en: The policy network is indeed the search's starting point. Without it, Monte Carlo tree search would have to blindly explore among 250 options — extremely inefficient. After training, our policy network's top five recommended moves include the actual move played by professional players over 85% of the time. This means the search can concentrate on the most promising paths. But the policy network alone — without search — plays at roughly amateur 5-dan level. Search is still necessary.

text.zh: 价值网络——能准确评估局面才是最核心的能力
text.en: The value network — accurately evaluating positions is the most core capability

text.zh: 从某种意义上，你说得对。围棋中最难的部分就是判断一个局面到底谁有优势。人类棋手需要几十年的经验才能建立起这种判断力。我们的价值网络通过学习数千万个对弈局面，达到了接近专业棋手的位置评估能力。在AlphaGo的搜索中，价值网络的评估和随机走子模拟（rollout）各贡献一半的评价，但价值网络的贡献通常更为关键。
text.en: In a sense, you're right. The hardest part of Go is judging who has the advantage in a position. Human players need decades of experience to build this judgment. Our value network, by learning from tens of millions of game positions, achieved position evaluation close to professional level. In AlphaGo's search, the value network's evaluation and random rollout simulation each contribute half of the assessment, but the value network's contribution is typically more critical.

text.zh: 蒙特卡洛树搜索——它把直觉和判断整合起来，做出最终决策
text.en: Monte Carlo tree search — it integrates intuition and judgment to make the final decision

text.zh: 搜索算法确实是把所有能力整合在一起的粘合剂。策略网络和价值网络各自都很强，但如果没有搜索来协调它们、来向前推演几步，棋力会大打折扣。搜索让AlphaGo能够「思考」——不仅仅是凭直觉出手，而是真的在内部模拟不同的未来走向，然后选择最有利的那一条。这种「想象未来」的能力，是搜索赋予的。
text.en: The search algorithm is indeed the glue that integrates all capabilities. The policy and value networks are each powerful, but without search to coordinate them and look ahead, playing strength drops significantly. Search lets AlphaGo 「think」 — not just play by intuition, but truly simulate different future paths internally, then choose the most favorable one. This ability to 「imagine the future」 is what search provides.

text.zh: 实际上，三个组件缺一不可。移除任何一个，AlphaGo的棋力都会大幅下降。它们的力量来自组合——策略网络缩小搜索空间，搜索算法展开深度推演，价值网络评估推演结果。这种组合产生了远超各部分之和的能力。
text.en: In reality, all three components are essential. Remove any one, and AlphaGo's strength drops dramatically. Their power comes from combination — the policy network narrows the search space, the search algorithm performs deep rollouts, and the value network evaluates the results. This combination produces capability far exceeding the sum of its parts.

text.zh: 那这些网络是怎么训练的呢？这是一个两阶段的过程。第一阶段：模仿学习。我们用人类职业棋手的三千万步对弈数据来训练策略网络——让它学会「像人类高手一样落子」。这一步让策略网络达到了大约业余高段的水平。
text.en: So how were these networks trained? It's a two-stage process. Stage one: imitation learning. We trained the policy network on thirty million moves from professional human games — teaching it to 「play like a human expert」. This step brought the policy network to roughly high-amateur level.

text.zh: 第二阶段：自我对弈强化学习。策略网络和自己下棋——左手和右手对弈。每一局棋结束后，赢的那一方的策略被强化，输的那一方的策略被弱化。经过数百万局自我对弈，策略网络超越了它的「人类老师」。它不再只是模仿人类，而是发现了人类从未使用过的策略。
text.en: Stage two: self-play reinforcement learning. The policy network plays against itself — left hand versus right hand. After each game, the winning side's strategy is reinforced, the losing side's is weakened. After millions of self-play games, the policy network surpassed its 「human teachers」. It was no longer just imitating humans; it had discovered strategies that humans had never used.

text.zh: AlphaGo的训练先模仿人类棋谱，然后通过自我对弈超越人类。你觉得「先模仿再创新」这个训练顺序有什么深意？
text.en: AlphaGo's training first imitated human games, then surpassed humans through self-play. What do you think is the deeper meaning of this 「imitate first, then innovate」 training sequence?

text.zh: 站在巨人的肩膀上——人类的经验是一个很好的起点，但不是终点
text.en: Standing on the shoulders of giants — human experience is a great starting point, but not the destination

text.zh: 说得非常好。人类几千年的围棋积累给了AlphaGo一个优秀的起点。从这个起点出发自我探索，比从零开始高效得多。（他停顿了一下，目光变得锐利）但这同时也带来了一个问题：人类的经验是否也是一种限制？如果人类从来没想到某种下法，AlphaGo是不是也会被困在人类的思维框架里？这个问题，我们会在下一课给出一个令人惊讶的答案。
text.en: Very well put. Thousands of years of human Go knowledge gave AlphaGo an excellent starting point. Self-exploration from that point is far more efficient than starting from zero. But — (he pauses, eyes sharpening) — this also raises a question: is human experience simultaneously a limitation? If humans never thought of a certain approach, could AlphaGo also be trapped within human cognitive frameworks? We'll give a surprising answer to this question next lesson.

text.zh: 从随机开始太慢了——先用人类数据给一个「热启动」可以大大加速学习
text.en: Starting from random is too slow — using human data for a 「warm start」 greatly accelerates learning

text.zh: 从工程角度，你完全正确。一个随机初始化的策略网络下出来的棋简直不忍直视，它可能把棋子下在最角落、完全没有意义的位置。用人类数据预训练之后，网络至少知道了围棋的基本模式，比如哪些位置通常值得落子、什么样的形状是好的。从这个基础上做自我对弈，比从一片混沌中开始要高效千百倍。
text.en: From an engineering perspective, you're absolutely right. A randomly initialized policy network plays moves that are painful to watch — placing stones in the farthest corner, completely meaningless positions. After pretraining with human data, the network at least knows Go's basic patterns — which positions are typically worth playing, what shapes are good. Self-play from this foundation is hundreds of times more efficient than starting from chaos.

text.zh: 模仿只是手段，自我对弈才是真正的突破——因为自我对弈可以无限产生新的训练数据
text.en: Imitation is just a means; self-play is the real breakthrough — because self-play can generate unlimited new training data

text.zh: 你切中了核心。人类棋谱的数量有限，但自我对弈能无限生成新的高质量数据。更重要的是，自我对弈产生的数据质量会不断提高。随着策略变强，对弈的水平也水涨船高，产生的训练数据也更有价值。这形成了一个自我强化的循环。你的这个观察，直接指向了我们下节课要讲的内容：一个完全不需要人类数据的系统。
text.en: You've hit the core. Human game records are limited in number, but self-play can generate unlimited new high-quality data. More importantly — the quality of self-play data continuously improves. As the policy gets stronger, the games get better, and the training data becomes more valuable. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle. Your observation points directly to what we'll discuss next lesson — a system that needs no human data at all.

text.zh: 模仿加上自我对弈——这个两阶段训练让AlphaGo达到了超越所有人类棋手的水平。但比赛中发生的一些事情，才真正让我意识到AlphaGo已经不只是在「模仿」人类了。
text.en: Imitation plus self-play — this two-stage training brought AlphaGo beyond all human players. But certain things that happened during the match were what truly made me realize AlphaGo was no longer just 「imitating」 humans.

text.zh: （声音微微颤动）第二局——2016年3月10日。AlphaGo执黑，下到了第37手。这一手棋落在了棋盘的右上方，一个极其罕见的位置。解说室的职业棋手们看到这步棋，第一反应是：「这是不是程序出了bug？」因为在人类的围棋理论中，这个时候没有人会下在那里。
text.en: (Voice trembling slightly) Game two — March 10th, 2016. AlphaGo played Black, and on move 37, it placed a stone in the upper right — an extremely unusual position. The professional players in the commentary room, upon seeing this move, first thought: 「Is this a bug in the program?」 Because in human Go theory, nobody would play there at that point.

text.zh: 但随着对局的推进，所有人都渐渐看明白了——那步棋是一着深远的布局。它影响了整个棋盘的走势，从全局的角度来看是一步极其精妙的棋。事后分析表明，策略网络给这步棋的概率只有万分之几，也就是说，按照人类棋谱学到的知识，它几乎不可能下在这里。但搜索算法在深入推演之后发现，这步棋的价值远高于所有「常规」选项。
text.en: But as the game progressed, everyone gradually understood — that move was a profound strategic placement. It influenced the entire board's direction and was, from a global perspective, an extraordinarily brilliant move. Post-game analysis showed the policy network gave this move only a few ten-thousandths of a percent probability — meaning that based on knowledge learned from human games, it would almost never play there. But the search algorithm, after deep exploration, discovered this move's value far exceeded all 「conventional」 options.

suggestedContent.zh: AlphaGo的三大核心组件：(1) 策略网络，它输出落子概率，提供「直觉」；(2) 价值网络，用于评估局面胜率，提供「判断力」；(3) 蒙特卡洛树搜索，负责整合直觉与判断，通过深度推演做出最终决策。训练流程是先用人类棋谱做模仿学习，再通过自我对弈强化学习来超越人类。第37手：搜索发现了策略网络（基于人类经验）认为概率极低的着法，这证明搜索与学习结合能够突破人类认知的边界。
suggestedContent.en: AlphaGo's three core components: (1) Policy network — outputs move probabilities, provides 「intuition」; (2) Value network — evaluates position win rate, provides 「judgment」; (3) Monte Carlo tree search — integrates intuition and judgment, makes final decisions after deep exploration. Training: first imitation learning from human games, then self-play RL to surpass humans. Move 37: search discovered a move the policy network (based on human experience) rated as near-zero probability, proving that search + learning can transcend human cognitive boundaries.

text.zh: AlphaGo的训练依赖人类棋谱数据作为起点。你觉得这种对人类数据的依赖是一种优势还是一种局限？
text.en: AlphaGo's training relied on human game data as a starting point. Do you think this dependence on human data is an advantage or a limitation?

text.zh: 是优势——人类几千年的围棋智慧是宝贵的先验知识
text.en: An advantage — thousands of years of human Go wisdom is invaluable prior knowledge

text.zh: 确实，人类棋谱让AlphaGo避免了从零学习的漫长过程。但我后来开始思考一个问题：人类棋谱中是否也包含了人类的偏见和盲区？如果人类从来没有发现某种走法，AlphaGo就不可能从棋谱中学到它。第37手之所以让我们震惊，正是因为搜索突破了人类经验的边界。这让我想到——如果我们完全放弃人类数据，会发生什么？
text.en: Indeed, human game records saved AlphaGo from the long process of learning from scratch. But I later began wondering: do human game records also contain human biases and blind spots? If humans never discovered a certain approach, AlphaGo couldn't learn it from games. Move 37 stunned us precisely because search broke through the boundary of human experience. This made me wonder — what would happen if we completely abandoned human data?

text.zh: 是局限——人类的下法可能并不是最优的，反而会给AI设置一个天花板
text.en: A limitation — human play might not be optimal, and could actually set a ceiling for the AI

text.zh: （眼中闪过兴奋的光）你的想法和我们后来的发现惊人地一致。如果AlphaGo的策略网络是在人类棋谱上训练的，那它的「直觉」本质上是人类的直觉。人类的直觉在很多情况下是出色的，但它也有盲区。如果我们能让系统从一张白纸开始，完全通过自我对弈来学习——它会发现什么？这个问题的答案……我们已经知道了。下节课我会告诉你们。
text.en: (Eyes flash with excitement) Your thinking aligns remarkably with what we later discovered. If AlphaGo's policy network was trained on human games, then its 「intuition」 is essentially human intuition. Human intuition is excellent in many cases, but it has blind spots. If we could let the system start from a blank slate, learning entirely through self-play — what would it discover? The answer to this question... we already know. I'll tell you next lesson.

text.zh: 是过渡手段——先依赖人类数据建立基础，最终目标应该是完全自主学习
text.en: A stepping stone — depend on human data to build a foundation first, but the ultimate goal should be fully autonomous learning

text.zh: 你描述的正是我们的研究路线图。AlphaGo是第一步，它证明了深度强化学习可以在围棋这样复杂的问题上超越人类。但我们真正追求的，是一个更大的目标：让AI能在没有任何人类知识的情况下，从零开始学习。就像一张白纸，只给它游戏规则。下节课要讲的AlphaGo Zero，就是这个目标的实现。
text.en: What you've described is exactly our research roadmap. AlphaGo was step one — proving deep RL can surpass humans on problems as complex as Go. But what we truly aspire to is a bigger goal: learning from scratch with zero human knowledge. A blank slate, with only the game rules. Next lesson — AlphaGo Zero — is the realization of that goal.

text.zh: 让我用一句话来总结AlphaGo的意义。它证明了一件很多人认为不可能的事情：在一个搜索空间超过宇宙原子数的问题上，将学习和搜索结合起来，可以达到超人的决策能力。这个原则不仅仅适用于围棋——它是通用的。
text.en: Let me summarize AlphaGo's significance in one sentence. It proved something many thought impossible: in a problem whose search space exceeds the atoms in the universe, combining learning with search can achieve superhuman decision-making. This principle doesn't just apply to Go — it's universal.

text.zh: 但我一直在想一个问题：AlphaGo之所以强大，有多少是因为它学到了人类几千年的围棋智慧，又有多少是因为它自己发现了新的智慧？如果我们剥离掉所有的人类知识，不给它任何棋谱，也不告诉它任何人类的围棋理论，它还能学会下棋吗？它能超越有人类知识帮助的版本吗？
text.en: But I keep thinking about a question: how much of AlphaGo's strength comes from learning thousands of years of human Go wisdom, and how much comes from discovering new wisdom on its own? If we strip away all human knowledge — give it no game records, tell it no human Go theory — can it still learn to play? Can it surpass the version that had human knowledge?

text.zh: （嘴角带着一种意味深长的微笑）答案是，可以。而且它做得更好，远远更好。下节课，我来告诉你们AlphaGo Zero的故事。这是一个从零开始、只用三天就超越了AlphaGo所有版本的系统，它彻底颠覆了我们对人类知识价值的认知。
text.en: (Smiling meaningfully) The answer is — yes. And it did better. Far, far better. Next lesson, I'll tell you the story of AlphaGo Zero — a system that started from scratch and surpassed all versions of AlphaGo in just three days. It overturned our understanding of the value of human knowledge.

text.zh: 西尔弗教授关掉了新闻画面，屏幕变成了一个静态的围棋棋盘。那是第二局的第37手，一颗黑子落在右上方一个看似不起眼的位置。他久久地看着那颗棋子，轻声说：「这步棋改变了很多人对围棋的理解。但真正改变我对AI理解的，是后来发生的事情。」他走向门口时，教室里一片安静。你看着屏幕上那颗孤独的黑子，忽然觉得，也许最深刻的智慧，不一定来自人类的传承，它也可能来自一张白纸上的自我探索。
text.en: Prof. Silver turns off the news footage, and the screen becomes a static Go board. It's Game Two, Move 37 — a black stone placed at a seemingly unremarkable position in the upper right. He gazes at that stone for a long moment and says softly: 「This move changed many people's understanding of Go. But what truly changed my understanding of AI was what came next」. As he walks to the door, the classroom is silent. You look at that solitary black stone on screen and suddenly feel that perhaps the deepest wisdom doesn't necessarily come from human tradition — it might also come from self-exploration on a blank page.
